reference.method: mpmath at 50 significant digits from the Double values the sheet holds; the Student t from the regularized incomplete beta, its quantile by bisection and Newton; the Binomial quantile by exact fractions

cases.name: Default portfolio
cases.purpose: The default example: a position of 1,000,000 with a daily volatility of 1% over 10 days, 99% VaR and ES, a Student t with 4 degrees of freedom; 100 loans with a default probability of 2% and a loss of 10,000 each.

cases.name: Expected shortfall at 97.5%
cases.purpose: ES at 97.5% next to the VaR at the same level: the ES is the larger of the two.

cases.name: Near the variance limit
cases.purpose: nu = 2.5, just above the limit of a finite variance: the matched scale s is small and the far tail of the Student t is much heavier than the Normal's.

cases.name: Thin tails
cases.purpose: nu = 200: the Student t at matched variance is close to the Normal.

cases.name: One day, zero mean
cases.purpose: A one-day horizon with a zero mean return: the VaR is the volatility times the quantile.

cases.name: Expected loss
cases.purpose: A negative mean return, so the mean loss is positive; the threshold 0 asks for the probability of any loss; the 90% default count is 1.

cases.name: Rare tail
cases.purpose: 99.99% over 20 days with nu = 3: the Student-t VaR is far beyond the Normal's, and a loss of 1,000,000 is many times likelier.
